story:
In the second summer of Morgana's war a highland clan came down from the north of Albion by sea, in long boats, with their women and their bard and their smith, because the bard had sung that the dead were walking on the colleges' burying isle and the clan had a quarrel with the dead older than the realm. They landed beside Little Haven, the one corner of Caldey the living still held, and built an outpost on the rise above it, and put their defenders on the wall, and have not gone home.

The Matron leads them. The clan does not have a chief; it has a matron, who decides who comes in and who stays out, and remembers. That is her office, as the highland clans keep it: to remember everyone who has crossed the clan, and how, and whether it was paid. A stranger who has done the clan no harm is let in and sold shields and armour and a song, and a stranger who has hunted the clan's people is not, and the Matron does not need to be told which a man is. Her maidens keep the stalls. Her defenders keep the wall. She keeps the tally.

The clan buries its own without rowans. The priests of the dead planted rowans round every grave on Caldey to keep the dead lying down, and the clan says that is a lowland custom and a coward's: a highland dead man who gets up will get up on the clan's side, and if he does not, his kin will lay him themselves. The fishermen of Little Haven think the clan is mad, and are very glad of it.

The Matron has never once struck first. She stands in the outpost among her people, unarmed by the look of her, and lets the world come to the gate; and when the world comes with a blade in its hand, the wall comes down to meet it, because the defenders are hers and she is theirs. The Clan Bard has a song about the night someone tried. It is short, and it has the stranger's name in it, which the Matron supplied.
legend: The Clan Matron is the level 54 head of the highland clan's outpost beside Little Haven on Caldey. She never aggros, and the whole Caldey Outpost faction starts neutral, so the clan is safe to walk through; what they sell you and how they treat you depends on your standing with them. Hitting her is a bad idea: the barbarian defenders (50s) and the other clan folk share her faction and come in, and every clan member you kill can sour your standing. No spells or styles in the data. There is no reason to kill her; she is listed here because she is a named 54. Respawn about 80 seconds.

loremasterTopic.text: The head of the highland [clan outpost] beside [little haven], come down from the north in the second summer of the war. Her office is to remember everyone who has crossed the clan and whether it was paid. She never strikes first; her defenders do it for her. The clan buries its own without rowans: a highland dead man who gets up gets up on the clan's side.

bookPage: From the Ledger of Little Haven, kept by Mordwywr, enchanter. Paid: to the Clan Matron, nothing, because she would not take it, for the clan's word that Little Haven may shelter behind the outpost wall when the dead come over the hill. I asked what the clan wanted in return. She said only that the village keep its tally honest, as she keeps hers. I asked what was in her tally. She said every name that ever owed the clan, and what for, and whether it was paid. I asked whether mine was in it. She said not yet. I have entered that as the best bargain in this ledger.
